primitives.verbatim_quote: The apparent drop-off in pitcher performance from one time through the order to the next, known as the Time Through the Order Penalty (TTOP), is often attributed to within-game batter learning.

primitives.name: Time Through the Order Penalty
primitives.verbatim_quote: The apparent drop-off in pitcher performance from one time through the order to the next, known as the Time Through the Order Penalty (TTOP), is often attributed to within-game batter learning.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: TTOP = difference in expected wOBA between consecutive TTOs; units: wOBA points.
primitives.assumptions: Batter learns incrementally with each encounter; pitch selection may adapt but is not the primary driver.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Late innings, high leverage situations, rare pitch sequences.

layer2.mapping: GSI: TTOP as a feature for player valuation adjustments; GSE: transition from 'early' to 'late' pitcher states.
layer2.telemetry: Change in wOBA per TTO bin, adjusted for confounders.

primitives.name: Running Average Quality Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The apparent drop-off in pitcher performance from one time through the order to the next, known as the Time Through the Order Penalty (TTOP), is often attributed to within-game batter learning.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x^{(b)}_i, x^{(p)}_i = scaled counts of outcomes; t_j = number of previous plate appearances; y_j = outcome indicator.
primitives.assumptions: Prior performance is informative about current ability; no season-long trends are modeled explicitly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: New players, small sample sizes, extreme streaks.

layer2.mapping: GSI: dynamic scaling factors for player ratings; GSE: state initialization for new batter-pitcher matchups.

primitives.name: Batting Adaptation Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: After the game, Cash justified his decision to pull Snell, remarking that he "didn't want Mookie [Betts] or [Corey] Seager seeing Blake a third time" (Rivera 2020).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Adaptation = increase in on-base percentage (OBP) or wOBA per additional TTO; units: percentage points.
primitives.assumptions: Learning is gradual and monotonic; individual differences exist but follow a common distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pitcher substitution mid-game, unusual defensive shifts, strategic intentional walks.

layer2.mapping: GSI: adaptation curves for projecting future performance; GSE: situational reasoning around batter readiness.
layer2.telemetry: Longitudinal change in OBP/wOBA vs. TTO count.

reasoning_traces.think:
We derive the TTOP as a discrete jump in a smooth latent function representing pitcher deterioration. Existing point estimates suffer from collider bias: managers remove poor-performing starters early, inflating apparent TTOP. Our Bayesian model corrects this by jointly modeling pitcher quality and removal decisions. The key insight is that TTOP is not an isolated effect but part of a continuous degradation process modulated by batter adaptation. This resolves the tension between Cash's tactical concern and the statistical evidence that TTOP is weak when controlling for confounders. The resulting operators enable precise probabilistic statements about when a pitcher's performance crosses critical thresholds.
